data.gender_notes: Asvika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Goddess Asvini, also known as the Ashvins or the Horse-born Twins in Hindu mythology, represents health, prosperity, and joy. The name Asvika is derived from the Sanskrit word 'asu' meaning 'horse' and 'vika' meaning 'born'. The name Asvika carries the meaning “Horse Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Asvika usually hope their child will grow to embody horse goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asvika total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The Asvins or the Horse-born Twins are revered in Hindu tradition as divine physicians. They often appear together to cure illnesses, bestow health, and bring joy. The name Asvika thus holds a deep connection with health, happiness, and well-being. It is also believed that the Asvins ensure the fertility of livestock, symbolizing prosperity in agriculture and animal husbandry.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Asvika holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the divine energies of the Asvini deities. This name not only evokes their protective and healing qualities but also symbolizes the power of faith and the importance of seeking divine intervention for physical and mental wellbeing. By carrying the name Asvika, one invokes the blessings and grace of the Asvini deities, drawing strength, courage, and resilience in our daily lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Asvika: Radiant as the horse, swift as the wind, embodying the spirit of freedom and strength.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'अस्वि' (Asva) meaning 'Horse'.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Asvika is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a princess. The name Asvika carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Princess Asvika was the daughter of King Shantanu and Satyavati. She was married to Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandavas.
